# An attained affine-root budget upper bound for mixed depth

This strengthens `candidate 4e07416b95553009`.
It is an upper bound and supplies necessary conditions at a critical
cap. It does not give the lower bound required by OC.

## 1. Setting and the clipped affine-root functional

Let d>=1 and let C be a bounded convex set in R^n times R^d with
compact integer fibers. Let P be the finite set of bases having
positive d-volume V_z=|C_z|. Other fibers have zero mass in this note.
Fix z_0 in P, y in C_(z_0), and a nonzero continuous normal u such that

    q=|C_(z_0) intersect {x:u.x>=u.y}|

is proper, 0<q<V_(z_0). Set k=q^(1/d), r_z=V_z^(1/d), and define

    Phi_k(b)=sum_{z in P}
       min(V_z,[k+b.(z-z_0)]_+^d),   b in R^n,        (1)

where [a]_+=max(a,0). Let D denote the raw mixed depth at (z_0,y).
Then

    D<=min_{b in R^n} Phi_k(b).                       (2)

In particular, if f is the ordinary raw depth of y in its source
fiber, then

    D<=min_b Phi_(f^(1/d))(b)<=|P|f.                 (3)

For f=0 the first minimum is zero, attained at b=0, and D=0 by the
previous constant-budget boundary argument. No zero-volume quantile
construction at the source is required in that case.

## 2. Construct a halfspace for every affine root budget

Fix b and write ell_z=k+b.(z-z_0), q_z=[ell_z]_+^d. Constrain only
the bases at which V_z>q_z. On such a fiber, if q_z>0 let h_z be
the unique proper upper-tail quantile of volume q_z in direction u.
If q_z=0, let h_z=max_{x in C_z}u.x and use the NONEMPTY supporting
face C_z intersect {u.x=h_z} as the zero-volume captured set. This
face is compact and nonempty because the whole fiber is compact.
In all cases define

    E_z=C_z intersect {u.x>=h_z},  |E_z|=q_z.

The source is constrained and has h_(z_0)=s:=u.y.

For any convex combination of constrained bases with barycenter z_0,
convexity of C and ordinary Brunn--Minkowski give

    sum_z lambda_z E_z
      subset C_(z_0) intersect {u.x>=sum_z lambda_z h_z},

    |sum_z lambda_z E_z|^(1/d)
       >=sum_z lambda_z q_z^(1/d)
       =sum_z lambda_z [ell_z]_+
       >=sum_z lambda_z ell_z=k.                    (4)

The version of BM in (4) permits nonempty lower-dimensional compact
convex summands and their zero volumes. It follows, for example, by
adding the same epsilon ball to each summand, applying the positive
volume inequality, and decreasing epsilon to zero. Compact convex
outer parallel sets decrease to the original compact convex set;
finite volume and continuity from above justify the volume limit.
This approximation concerns only ordinary compact bodies inside this
one finite inequality, and changes no selected mixed-integer point.
In (4) not all summands with positive weight can have zero budgets,
since their weighted root sum is at least k>0.

The source tail at the threshold sum lambda_z h_z has volume at
least q=k^d. Its proper q-quantile is s, so that threshold is at most s.
The finite affine-majorant lemma proved in the constant-budget note
therefore supplies a vector a with

    h_z<=s+a.(z-z_0)

on all constrained bases. The genuine ambient halfspace

    H={ (z,x):u.x>=s+a.(z-z_0) }

contains (z_0,y) and captures at most q_z at each constrained base.
At every unconstrained base, its capture is at most V_z<=q_z.
Zero-volume fibers contribute zero. Consequently its mixed mass
is at most Phi_k(b). The depth infimum gives D<=Phi_k(b) for every b.

This proof does not require b to equal the actual integer part a of
the constructed normal. The first parametrizes a volume-root budget;
the second is obtained from finite quantile feasibility. Identifying
the two without proof would be incorrect.

## 3. The budget infimum is attained

The function in (1) is continuous but generally not convex or coercive.
Nevertheless its infimum is attained. Here is a finite-dimensional
argument that does not assume bounded affine coefficients.

Let E be the affine subspace of evaluation vectors

    x=(k+b.(z-z_0))_(z in P) in R^P.

Partition P into three status sets L,I,U and consider the closed cell

    x in E,
    x_z<=0 on L, 0<=x_z<=r_z on I, x_z>=r_z on U.

These finitely many closed cells cover E; overlaps at their boundaries
cause no problem. On a nonempty cell, the objective is exactly

    sum_{z in I} x_z^d + sum_{z in U}V_z.             (5)

Project the cell to the coordinates x_I. Its image is a closed
polyhedron and is contained in the compact box product_I[0,r_z].
For completeness, closedness here is the specific finite-polyhedron
fact: eliminate one real variable from finitely many nonstrict affine
inequalities by pairing each lower bound on that variable with each
upper bound. The resulting finitely many nonstrict inequalities are
equivalent to existence of a finite value of the eliminated variable;
if only one side is bounded, choose a finite value beyond those finitely
many bounds. Repeated elimination proves the assertion, also for an
affine subspace described by pairs of inequalities.

Thus (5) attains its minimum on this projected compact set. Every
projected point has an associated finite evaluation vector and finite
b by the definition of the projection and E. If I is empty, the
objective is constant on the nonempty cell and is already attained.
Taking the smallest of the finitely many cell minima proves attainment
in (2). Coordinates in L or U, and the coefficient vector b itself,
need not have been bounded along an arbitrary minimizing sequence.

To deduce (3), choose an attaining ordinary depth normal. For positive
f it has a proper cap because f<=V_(z_0)/2. Apply (2) and compare with
the constant budget b=0. The f=0 case was separated in the statement.

## 4. Consequence for affine captured-volume roots at a critical cap

Suppose an actual depth-attaining nonvertical cap through (z_0,y)
has captured roots

    a_z=a_0+ell.(z-z_0),  0<a_z<r_z

in every positive-volume fiber. No homothety of the cap shapes is
needed for this assertion. Its raw mass is Q=sum_z a_z^d, and its
own cap has q=a_0^d. Formula (2) gives

    Q=D<=min_b Phi_(a_0)(b)<=Phi_(a_0)(ell)=Q.

Hence ell is a GLOBAL minimizer of the clipped affine functional.
Because every displayed root lies strictly between its clipping
boundaries, differentiation on this open cell gives

    sum_z (z-z_0)a_z^(d-1)=0.                        (6)

For d>=2 this implies the exact polynomial deficit identity

    |P|a_0^d-Q
      =sum_z(a_0-a_z)^2
           sum_{j=0}^{d-2}(j+1)a_0^(d-2-j)a_z^j>=0. (7)

Indeed the affine expression and (6) give
sum_z(a_z-a_0)a_z^(d-1)=0. Sum the elementary identity
x^d-y^d-dy^(d-1)(x-y)
=(x-y)^2 sum_{j=0}^{d-2}(j+1)x^(d-2-j)y^j
with x=a_0 and y=a_z. For d=1 equation (6) reads
sum_z(z-z_0)=0, and affinity directly gives Q=|P|a_0.

Thus the necessary root-weight stationarity and deficit formula in
the affine homothetic-cap branch also follow from actual convexity,
depth criticality, and affine proper captured-volume roots alone.
The global clipped-functional conclusion controls competing root
budget cells as well; it does not establish actual optimality from
a merely stationary polynomial or from proposed roots.

## Scope

All measures in this note are d-dimensional fiber volumes, and the
source fiber is full-dimensional in R^d. No extension to varying
intrinsic direction spaces is asserted here. Zero-volume actual fibers
may remain in S but carry no mass. Every constructed halfspace has
nonzero continuous normal and is closed; its boundaries carry zero
d-volume on positive fibers. The result is independent of lattice
completeness beyond the actual convex interpolation of the sampled
fibers. It is an upper bound and a criticality constraint, not an OC
lower bound or a claimed global solution.
